The hepatic metabolism and excretion of PCBs in male Sprague-Daweley rats was investigated after dosing with a commercial PCB mixture (Clophen A 50) and that the formation of PCB methylsulphonyls (MeSO2) metabolites was determined.

1) the hepatic concentration of PCBs decreased in rat liver after dosing with a PCB mixture, and that 2) the hepatic concentrations of MeSO2- PCB metabolites were highest after 2 weeks and thereafter decreased.

the development and validation of a method for the analysis of MeSO2- PCBs in rat liver.
the metabolism and the synthesis of MeSO2- PCBs in rat liver.
the identification, quantification, and synthesis of MeSO2- PCBs in rat liver after treatment with PCBs.

MeSO2-CB153 and MeSO2-CBs 101, 87 and 149 are the most important MeSO2- PCBs in rat liver after treatment with Clophen A 50.

the MeSO2- PCBs are formed as metabolites of the parent PCBs and that the relative concentrations of these metabolites are influenced by the PCBs present in the liver and the time elapsed after dosing.

the MeSO2-formation in rat liver is dependent on time and congener structure, and that the MeS-PCBs are not the immediate metabolites of the parent PCBs.

The main takeaway from our work is that
PCBs are metabolized by the P450 system in rat liver to MeSO2- PCBS.
the MeSO2- PCBs are not only formed as a minor metabolite of the PCBs, but that they are formed at high levels.
